method: Receiver sensitivity is the thermal noise power in the receiver bandwidth plus the receiver noise figure plus the signal-to-noise ratio the demodulator needs: Pmin = 10 log10(k T B) + NF + SNR, reported in dBm with k = 1.380649e-23 J/K, T in kelvin, B in hertz and NF and SNR in dB. At the reference temperature of 290 K the thermal noise density is about -173.98 dBm/Hz, which is the familiar -174 dBm/Hz figure. The noise floor in the chosen bandwidth is reported separately, together with the equivalent RMS voltage across a matched 50 ohm load from V = sqrt(P R) and the signal power in watts. The reference table recomputes the noise floor and sensitivity for 3 kHz, 12.5 kHz, 25 kHz, 200 kHz, 1 MHz and 20 MHz using the entered noise figure, SNR and temperature. Bandwidth accepts hertz, kilohertz or megahertz and is limited to 1 THz, noise figure to 0-100 dB, required SNR to -100 to 100 dB (negative values model spreading and coding gain) and temperature to 1-10,000 K. The estimate assumes a flat noise figure across the band, a receiver noise figure that already includes feedline loss ahead of the receiver, and a matched 50 ohm system for the voltage; it does not model interference, phase noise, spurs, fading, coding gain, antenna noise or a complete link budget, and it runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: H. T. Friis, Noise Figures of Radio Receivers, Proceedings of the IRE, 1944 (noise figure definition)
ITU-R P.372, Radio Noise (reference noise temperature and noise density)
D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, 4th ed. (thermal noise, noise figure and receiver sensitivity)
